product_name: Drontal™ Plus Broad Spectrum Anthelmintic Tablets

indication.text: Removal of tapeworms (Dipylidium caninum, Taenia pisiformis, Echinococcus granulosus, Echinococcus multilocularis), hookworms, ascarids and whipworms in dogs; this supplement adds the E. multilocularis claim.
indication.quote: Tapeworms (Dipylidium caninum, Taenia pisiformis, Echinococcus granulosus, and Echinococcus multilocularis), hookworms (Ancylostoma caninum and Uncinaria stenocephala), ascarids (Toxocara canis and Toxascaris leonina), and whipworms (Trichuris vulpis).

dose_regimen.dose: Small dogs (2-25 lbs.): 0.5 to 2.5 tablets by body weight chart; separate chart for medium and large dogs
dose_regimen.route: Oral (tablets given directly by mouth or offered in a small amount of food)
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: Small-dog tablet contains 22.7 mg praziquantel, 22.7 mg pyrantel base and 113.4 mg febantel (medium/large tablet 68.0/68.0/340.2 mg); not for use in dogs weighing less than 2 lbs or puppies less than 3 weeks of age; fasting neither necessary nor recommended
dose_regimen.quote: Table 1. Drontal(TM) Plus Tablets for Small Dogs*(2-25 lbs.) Body Wt. (lbs.) Number of Tablets 2 - 4 0.5 5 - 7 1.0 8 - 12 1.5 13 - 18 2.0 19 - 25 2.5

effectiveness.design: No new studies; the E. multilocularis claim is extrapolated from laboratory data in the Droncit (praziquantel) FOI Summary (NADA 111-798) plus the absence of interference from pyrantel/febantel shown in the original Drontal Plus approval
effectiveness.result: Droncit reported 100% efficacious against E. granulosus and E. multilocularis; praziquantel in Drontal Plus concluded to be as efficacious as Droncit against E. multilocularis
effectiveness.quote: The laboratory data described in the FOI Summary of NADA 111-798 indicate that Droncit (praziquantel) Tablets [NADA 111-798, 58 FR 42852-3, Aug. 12, 1993] is 100% efficacious against both E. granulosus and E. multilocularis.

notes: Supplemental approval (1996) adding Echinococcus multilocularis to the label. Contains no new animal studies: effectiveness is argued by cross-reference to NADA 111-798 (Droncit), and target animal safety and human safety are cross-referenced to the original 1994 Drontal Plus FOI Summary (foi_id 3619). Dose is expressed only as body-weight tablet charts (Table 1 small dogs quoted; Table 2 medium/large dogs 26-120 lbs, 1.0-4.0 tablets, not quoted). No PK or adverse-reaction data in this summary.

product_name: Drontal™ Plus Broad Spectrum Anthelmintic Tablets

indication.text: Removal of tapeworms (Dipylidium caninum, Taenia pisiformis, Echinococcus granulosus), hookworms (Ancylostoma caninum, Uncinaria stenocephala), ascarids (Toxocara canis, Toxascaris leonina) and whipworms (Trichuris vulpis) in dogs.
indication.quote: Drontal™ Plus Broad Spectrum Anthelmintic Tablets are indicated for the removal of the following intestinal parasites in dogs:

dose_regimen.dose: 5 mg/kg (2.27 mg/lb) each of praziquantel and pyrantel base + 25 mg/kg (11.35 mg/lb) febantel
dose_regimen.route: Oral (directly by mouth or offered in the food)
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: Two tablet sizes dosed by body-weight chart; not for use in dogs weighing less than 2 lbs or puppies less than 3 weeks of age
dose_regimen.quote: Drontal Plus Tablets: 5 mg/kg (2.27 mg/lb) of praziquantel and pyrantel base + 25 mg/kg (11.35 mg/lb) febantel (The formulation to be marketed)

target_animal_safety.duration: 3 consecutive days (3 times the labeled single-dose duration)

findings.finding: Dose-related vomition and non-formed stools were the only clinical signs
findings.quote: Clinical signs were dose related and consisted of vomition and non-formed stools.

findings.finding: No hematology/clinical chemistry trends except one 3X dog with elevated SGPT, SGOT, GGT and CPK at 6 days post-treatment
findings.quote: No post- treatment trends were seen for the group mean values for the hematology and clinical chemistry parameters when compared to the pretreatment values or to those of nontreated controls with the exception of one dog in Group III which had elevated SGPT (549), SGOT (239), GGT (15) and CPK (285) readings at 6 days post- treatment.

findings.finding: No treatment-related necropsy or histological findings
findings.quote: None of the findings at necropsy or upon histological examination were judged to be treatment related.

findings.finding: Table 10 row for the 5X group (columns: number of animals, treatment rate, clinical observations)
findings.quote: 4 5 X Use Rate for 3 Days Vomition in 3 and non-formed stool in 1

findings.finding: Separate drug tolerance test: single 10X dose (2 treated dogs, 1 placebo) induced vomition only
findings.quote: It was concluded from this study that a single treatment of dogs with this praziquantel/pyrantel/febantel formulation at 10 times the label use rate can induce vomition without other adverse clinical effects.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: M. Kohlenberg also conducted a general safety study in 14 dogs using the 68.0/68.0/340.2 mg tablet. Two of the dogs, Group 1, were nontreated controls. Groups II, III and IV (4 animals/group) received 1, 3 and 5 times the recommend use rate, respectively, for 3 consecutive days (3 times the duration of treatment).

effectiveness.design: Pivotal clinical trial at five U.S. veterinary clinics in naturally infected dogs (each animal its own control; tapeworm clearance checked on Days 5-7 and nematode egg count reduction at 7-10 days), supported by four blinded, placebo-controlled laboratory necropsy studies in 176 dogs (Studies 1-4)
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Post-treatment percent reduction of mean egg counts and percent of cases cleared to zero (clinical trial); controlled percent efficacy from worm counts at necropsy 7 days after treatment (laboratory studies)
effectiveness.result: Clinical trial (Table 7): T. vulpis 94.5% egg reduction (98 infections), T. pisiformis and D. caninum 100%, A. caninum 97.2%, T. canis 89.5%. Laboratory: combined Studies 1 and 4 gave 94.0% T. vulpis removal vs 0% for praziquantel+pyrantel; 99.6-100% A. caninum, 99.8% U. stenocephala, 97.81% T. leonina, 100% T. pisiformis
effectiveness.quote: The investigators treated a total of 103 purebred and mixed-breed dogs (48 males and 55 females) with Drontal Plus Tablets. No side effects following treatment (excellent rating) were reported for any of the 103 cases.

adverse_reactions.term: Any side effect, Drontal Plus clinical trial (103 dogs, excellent rating for all)
adverse_reactions.quote: No side effects following treatment (excellent rating) were reported for any of the 103 cases.

adverse_reactions.term: Overall safety rated excellent (no side effects), Drontal Plus field safety confirmation
adverse_reactions.quote: The clinical veterinarians rated overall safety as excellent (no side effects observed) for all of the treatments (100%).

adverse_reactions.term: Side effects in laboratory efficacy studies (placebo-controlled)
adverse_reactions.quote: No side effects were observed after treatment.

notes: Original approval (1994). Effectiveness rests on four laboratory studies (176 dogs) plus a 103-dog clinical trial; the clinical trial quote is used because it states n. Efficacy tables were flattened by PDF extraction (percentages and dog counts on separate lines), so per-parasite figures are given in the result field rather than quoted. Target animal safety: the margin-of-safety study is the 14-dog General Safety Evaluation (1X/3X/5X for 3 days); a 3-dog 10X single-dose tolerance test and several corroborative praziquantel/pyrantel and puppy tolerance studies are also described. Adverse-reaction counts use treated=null where the figure is not a digit in the quote (e.g. 'any of the 103 cases'). No PK data.

indication.text: Treatment and control of roundworms, hookworms, whipworms and tapeworms (Taenia pisiformis) in adult dogs (including pregnant bitches) and puppies six weeks of age or older.
indication.quote: PANACUR®-C granules are indicated for use in adult dogs (including pregnant bitches) and puppies, six weeks of age or older, for the treatment and control of roundworms (Toxocara canis, Toxascaris leonina), hookworms (Ancylostoma caninum, Uncinaria stenocephala), whipworms (Trichuris vulpis) and tapeworms (Taenia pisiformis).

dose_regimen.route: Oral, mixed with a small amount of the usual food
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: Three (3) days in a row; packets of 1 g, 2 g and 4 g dosed by body weight
dose_regimen.quote: The daily dose for PANACUR®-C is 50 mg/kg (22.7 mg/lb.) of body weight.

notes: Supplemental approval (2002) changing the 22.2% granule packets from Rx to OTC status (PANACUR-C). The summary contains no studies: effectiveness and safety are stated to be unaffected and are cross-referenced to the original approval dated 27 October 1983. Agency conclusions note that the original Rx status reflected a hepatotoxicity concern and that post-approval marketing experience has not shown a pattern of liver disease. No PK, TAS or adverse-reaction data.

indication.text: Control of internal parasites (ascarids Toxocara cati/Toxascaris leonina, hookworms Ancylostoma spp., tapeworms Taenia spp. as listed per species) in wild Felidae (lion, tiger, cheetah, puma, panther, leopard, jaguar) and Ursidae (grizzly, polar and black bears).
indication.quote: Panacur® (fenbendazole) is used for control of the following internal parasites in the families Felidae and Ursidae.

dose_regimen.route: Orally, mixed with food or as a top dressing
dose_regimen.quote: Felidae and Ursidae: 10 mg/kg/bw daily for 3 days

target_animal_safety.duration: Felidae dosed for six (6) days; polar bears for four (4) days

findings.finding: Periods of inappetence in one jaguar and the lion after initial consumption at ten times the recommended level (extreme ambient heat noted as a possible factor)
findings.quote: In one jaguar and the lion, there were periods of inappentence (sic) following the initial consumption of fenbendazole at ten times the recommended level.

findings.finding: No adverse reactions at exaggerated doses; only remarkable finding was possible refusal of the drug
findings.quote: The only remarkable finding is that the overdosed animal may not consume the drug.

findings.finding: Safety parameters limited to clinical observation; no necropsies
findings.quote: Due to the nature of the study, safety parameters were limited to those which could be obtained from clinical observation of the animals.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Five big cats, including two jaguars, one puma, one lion, and one Siberian tiger representing both sexes and ranging in age from 2 to 15 years of age were dosed with the drug. Additionally, three polar bears ranging in age from 7 to 9 years of age and representing both sexes were dosed with 100 mg/kg/bw of the drug for four (4) days. The Felidae were dosed with 100 mg/kg/bw for six (6) days.

effectiveness.design: Six pivotal zoo field trials (three in Felidae with 29 animals, three in Ursidae with 26 animals) using each animal as its own control by comparing pre- and post-treatment fecal ova counts; three corroborative trials; no statistics applied
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Reduction in fecal parasite ova counts post-treatment
effectiveness.result: 100% reduction in Ancylostoma and Taenia spp. ova where observed; 100% reduction in ascarid ova in most bear studies and 80% in one (bears dosed 2 days, hence 3-day label); pronounced pre/post difference in greater than 90% of animals tested
effectiveness.quote: There are three studies involving 29 members of the family Felidae and three studies involving 26 members of the family Ursidae.

adverse_reactions.quote: There were several reports of loose stools among the pumas ingesting the Panacur® granules.
There were several reports of loose stools among the bears ingesting the Panacur® granules.

notes: Supplemental approval (1994) for zoo Felidae and Ursidae, NOT dogs (species_class recorded as stated). Subjects are lions, tigers, cheetahs, pumas, jaguars, leopards, panthers and bears, so n_dogs is null and animal counts are in the design field. Safety study: 5 big cats at 100 mg/kg for 6 days and 3 polar bears at 100 mg/kg for 4 days (10X the 10 mg/kg label dose); the summary also describes this as 'Large cats offered 5X the dose for twice the duration and polar bears dosed at 10X', so both multiples are listed. n_animals left null because 'Five' and 'three' appear as words, not digits, in the design quote. No PK data; adverse reactions have no counts.

indication.text: Treatment and control of adult Toxocara canis, Ancylostoma caninum, Trichuris vulpis and Dipylidium caninum, and prevention of heartworm disease caused by Dirofilaria immitis, in adult dogs.
indication.quote: For the treatment and control of adult Toxocara canis (roundworm), Ancylostoma caninum (hookworm), Trichuris vulpis (whipworm), and Dipylidium caninum (tapeworm), and for the prevention of heartworm disease caused by Dirofilaria immitis in adult dogs.

dose_regimen.dose: Minimum 100 mg fenbendazole, 6 mcg ivermectin and 5 mg praziquantel per kg body weight
dose_regimen.quote: PANACUR Plus Soft Chews should be administered orally at monthly intervals at the recommended minimum dose level of 100 mg fenbendazole, 6 mcg ivermectin, and 5 mg praziquantel per kg of body weight.

target_animal_safety.duration: Once every two weeks for a total of six treatments (Days 0, 14, 28, 42, 56, 70); 77-day study

findings.finding: No clinically relevant treatment-related changes in food consumption, clinical pathology, necropsy or histopathology; all dogs healthy and gained weight
findings.quote: There were no clinically relevant treatment related changes in food consumption, hematology, clinical chemistries, coagulation parameters, urinalyses, necropsies, or histopathology.

findings.finding: Gastrointestinal signs (soft feces, diarrhea, vomiting) within 24 hours of dosing in all groups
findings.quote: The primary clinical signs were gastrointestinal reactions, including soft feces, diarrhea and vomiting, observed within 24 hours of dosing in all groups.

findings.finding: Increased vomiting 4 hours post-dose in the 5X group on 3 of 6 dosing days
findings.quote: A significant increase in vomiting (p = 0.06) was observed 4 hours post-dosing in the 5X group on 3 out of 6 dosing days.

findings.finding: Ivermectin-sensitive Collie study (Study 2045-013-01, 16 Collies at 0X/1X/3X/5X of the maximum Shetland Sheepdog exposure): mild mydriasis in one 5X dog only
findings.quote: A mild ivermectin toxicity reported as mydriasis was observed in one dog treated with the 5X dose as a single observation 8 hours post-treatment lasting 1 hour.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Twenty four 16 ± 1 week-old Beagles (12 males and 12 females), weighing 4.7 to 6.75 kg (10.34 to 14.85 pounds) on Day -1, were blocked by weight and randomized to one of four treatment groups.

effectiveness.design: Eight controlled laboratory dose-confirmation studies (single oral dose, placebo control, necropsy worm/scolex counts on Day 7 or 12, or Day 125 for heartworm), several including non-interference arms with single actives: T. canis natural (20 dogs) and induced (12); A. caninum natural (24) and induced (40); T. vulpis induced (20) and natural (40); D. caninum natural (20 and 40); D. immitis induced (20 and 40). No effectiveness field study; a 106-dog field safety/palatability study was conducted
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent effectiveness from geometric mean worm counts at necropsy versus control (threshold 90%)
effectiveness.result: T. canis 94.8% (natural) and 92.9% (induced); A. caninum 94.6% and 96.2%; T. vulpis 99.2% and 99.6%; D. caninum 100% in both studies; D. immitis 100% in both studies. Single actives were not effective against the non-target parasites (e.g. praziquantel 0% vs A. caninum; ivermectin 76.4% and praziquantel 27.8% vs T. vulpis; fenbendazole and ivermectin 0% vs D. caninum)
effectiveness.quote: The results of the worm counts at necropsy demonstrate that the control dogs were adequately infected with T. canis, the geometric mean worm count for the PANACUR Plus Soft Chew group was significantly less than the geometric mean worm count of the control group (p <0.001), and the PANACUR Plus Soft Chew was 94.8% (≥ 90%) effective against natural T. canis infections.

adverse_reactions.term: Death/euthanasia after dark diarrhea and dehydration (one dog, D. caninum non-interference laboratory study; pre-existing subclinical disease)
adverse_reactions.quote: One dog treated with the PANACUR Plus Soft Chews developed dark diarrhea, dehydration and was euthanized six days after treatment.

notes: Original approval (2008). No PK section. Target animal safety: margin-of-safety study 2045-003-01 in 24 Beagles at 1X/3X/5X of the maximum toy-breed exposure dose every 2 weeks for 6 doses (Table 11 mg/kg levels: 1X = 324 mg/kg fenbendazole, 19.3 mcg/kg ivermectin, 16.4 mg/kg praziquantel); n_animals expressed as '12 males and 12 females' because 'Twenty four' is spelled out in the design quote. A separate Collie ivermectin-sensitivity study (16 dogs) is summarised in findings. Effectiveness has no field study; n_dogs left null and per-study counts are in design; the quoted result is the first pivotal T. canis study. Adverse reaction rows are from the uncontrolled 106-dog field safety study (Table 9, N = 105, single column: number of dogs and percent); hypersalivation 1 (1.0) omitted. Palatability was not demonstrated in that study (59-68% voluntary acceptance).

indication.text: Control of postoperative pain associated with surgical procedures in dogs.
indication.quote: For the control of postoperative pain associated with surgical procedures in dogs.

dose_regimen.route: Topical (transdermal) to the dorsal scapular area
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: Applied 2 to 4 hours prior to surgery; a single application provides analgesia for 4 days
dose_regimen.quote: The dosage of RECUVYRA is 1.2 mg/lb (2.7 mg/kg) applied topically to the dorsal scapular area 2 to 4 hours prior to surgery. A single application provides analgesia for 4 days.

pharmacokinetics.value: Plasma fentanyl above 1 ng/mL over the 50 hour observation period
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Dogs, pilot dose-finding study T8F1090406; 2.6 and 3.9 mg/kg transdermal doses applied about 12 hours before ACL transection surgery (n=8 per group); marked between- and within-subject variability
pharmacokinetics.quote: Plasma concentrations remained above 1 ng/mL for the 2.6 and 3.9 mg/kg doses over the 50 hour observation period.

pharmacokinetics.value: Plasma fentanyl concentrations doubled from the first to the third dosing interval (accumulation with repeated dosing)
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Dogs, margin-of-safety study ARDG01-C-03; 2.6, 5.2 and 7.8 mg/kg topical to ventral abdomen every 4 days for 3 doses
pharmacokinetics.quote: Plasma fentanyl concentrations doubled from the first to the third dosing interval. Fentanyl concentrations appeared to show accumulation with successive doses in all treated groups.

pharmacokinetics.value: More rapid rise and decline in plasma fentanyl after dorsal scapular application than after ventral abdominal application
pharmacokinetics.conditions: Dogs, pharmacokinetic application-site study 021591 (Figure 1; no numeric values given)
pharmacokinetics.quote: The results of a pharmacokinetic application site study (021591) showed that administration to the dorsal scapular region allows for a more rapid rise and decline in fentanyl plasma concentrations as compared to that seen when fentanyl transdermal solution is applied to the ventral abdominal region (Figure 1).

pharmacokinetics.value: Half-life of 23.3 hours for the decline in fentanyl transferable from treated dog skin to a cotton glove (not a plasma half-life)
pharmacokinetics.conditions: User-safety glove-transfer study in dogs; 4.25% of dose recovered immediately after application, about 2% at 24 h and 1% at 48 h
pharmacokinetics.quote: The amount of fentanyl transferred declined over time with an estimated half-life of 23.3 hours.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: HUMAN volunteers (user safety section), exploratory human formulation of transdermal fentanyl solution vs DURAGESIC patch; not dog data
pharmacokinetics.quote: The mean fentanyl Cmax for arm, thigh, and patch were 0.318, 0.0975, and 0.545 ng/mL respectively.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: HUMAN volunteers (user safety section), transdermal fentanyl solution applied to arm or thigh; not dog data
pharmacokinetics.quote: The mean time to reach maximal plasma concentration (Tmax) for transdermal fentanyl solution was 34 hours (ranged from 18 to 96 hours).

target_animal_safety.duration: Every 4 days for a total of 3 doses (Days 0, 4, 8); 12-day study
target_animal_safety.n_animals: 8 dogs per dose group (16 male, 16 female)

findings.finding: Three deaths (two 2X dogs, one 3X dog) between the second and third doses from endotoxic shock secondary to severe gastrointestinal stasis with hypothermia and sedation
findings.quote: Three dogs died as a result of transdermal fentanyl administration. Death was due to endotoxic shock produced by severe gastrointestinal stasis complicated by continued hypothermia and sedation. All deaths occurred between the second and third doses. Two dogs (2X group) died on days 4 and 7, and the third dog (3X group) died on day 5.

findings.finding: Severe hypothermia (lowest 90.9-93.2 F), bradycardia and decreased respiratory rate in the dogs that died
findings.quote: All 3 dogs had severe hypothermia (body temperature < 98° F), with the lowest temperatures ranging from 90.9-93.2° F. The three dogs had bradycardia (heart rate < 60 beats per minute) and decreased respiratory rates.

findings.finding: Narrow margin of safety concluded
findings.quote: Administration of topical RECUVYRA every 4 days at 2.6, 5.2, and 7.8 mg/kg (1X, 2X, and 3X the clinical dose) for 3 doses showed a narrow margin of safety.

findings.finding: Spectrum of treatment effects: sedation, hypothermia, bradycardia, respiratory depression, dehydration, weight loss, decreased food consumption, GI signs
findings.quote: RECUVYRA caused variable levels of sedation that were sometimes profound, severe hypothermia, bradycardia, respiratory depression, dehydration, weight loss, decreased food consumption, blood in the feces, lack of feces, diarrhea,

findings.finding: Bone marrow changes suggestive of increased white blood cell demand (increased myeloid:erythroid ratios, most marked at 2X and 3X)
findings.quote: Results showed changes suggestive of an increased demand for white blood cells.

findings.finding: Naloxone reversal study (Study 021590, 24 Beagles, 5X = 13 mg/kg overdose): hourly IM naloxone temporarily reversed narcotic effects
findings.quote: Hourly administrations of 0.04 and 0.16 mg/kg IM naloxone were effective at temporarily reversing the narcotic effects of a 5X overdose (13 mg/kg) of a transdermal fentanyl solution applied to the ventral abdomen of dogs.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: To evaluate the margin of safety of RECUVYRA when administered to healthy adult mongrel dogs (eight dogs per group) at 0, 2.6, 5.2, and 7.8 mg/kg (0, 1, 2, and 3 times the dose) as a topical application administered every 4 days for a total of 3 doses. b. Description of Test Animals: Thirty-two purpose bred laboratory mongrel dogs 1-2 years of age (16 male, 16 female), 8 dogs per dose group.

effectiveness.design: Active-controlled (oxymorphone hydrochloride SC before surgery, at extubation and every 6 h through 90 h), double-masked, multi-center non-inferiority field study in 251 client-owned dogs (124 fentanyl, 127 oxymorphone) undergoing cruciate repair surgery (ARDG01-C-01); a parallel soft tissue surgery study (ARDG01-C-02) enrolled another 251 dogs (125 fentanyl, 126 oxymorphone)
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Dropout (treatment failure) rate due to lack of pain control (modified Glasgow Composite Pain Scale score of 8 or more) or opioid reversal with naloxone; non-inferiority if one-sided upper 95% bound of the RECUVYRA minus oxymorphone difference was below 15%
effectiveness.result: Orthopedic study: dropout 1.61% RECUVYRA vs 5.56% oxymorphone, upper bound -1.0%, non-inferior. Soft tissue study: dropout 1.60% vs 8.00%, upper bound -3.1%, non-inferior. Sedation score means were lower with RECUVYRA at all time points
effectiveness.quote: The dropout rate in the RECUVYRA treatment group was 1.61%, and the dropout rate in the oxymorphone treatment group was 5.56%. The one-sided upper 95% confidence bound was -1.0%, which is less than 15%. Therefore, based on dropout rate, RECUVYRA is non-inferior to oxymorphone.

adverse_reactions.quote: Adverse reactions were reported in 13 RECUVYRA-treated dogs (10.5%) and 32 oxymorphone-treated dogs (25.2%).

adverse_reactions.term: Emesis (orthopedic study, Table 4a; columns fentanyl n, %, oxymorphone n, %)
Any adverse reaction (soft tissue field study)
adverse_reactions.quote: Adverse reactions were reported in 31 RECUVYRA -treated dogs (24.8%) and 52 oxymorphone-treated dogs (41.3%).

notes: Original approval (2012). The summary has no dedicated PK section; dog plasma data are descriptive only (no Cmax/AUC/half-life values in dogs), so the two numeric Cmax/Tmax entries are HUMAN volunteer data from the user-safety section and are flagged as such in conditions; the 23.3 h 'half-life' is the decline of fentanyl transferable to a glove from treated dogs, not a plasma half-life. Target animal safety quotes the margin-of-safety study (32 mongrel dogs, 0/1X/2X/3X every 4 days x3, ventral abdomen); a 16-week repeat-dose study (PRO01-C-01) and two field safety studies are also in the section but not extracted. Effectiveness: two active-controlled field studies of 251 dogs each; n_dogs is null because the quoted result sentence does not contain the enrolment number (251 appears in a separate sentence). Adverse-reaction table rows (Table 4a orthopedic study, N=124 fentanyl vs N=127 oxymorphone) are quoted as flattened rows with column order given in term.

indication.text: Control of pain and inflammation associated with osteoarthritis and control of postoperative pain and inflammation associated with soft-tissue surgery in dogs (this supplement adds the soft-tissue surgery indication).
indication.quote: PREVICOX (firocoxib) Chewable Tablets are indicated for the control of pain and inflammation associated with osteoarthritis and for the control of postoperative pain and inflammation associated with soft-tissue surgery in dogs.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: As needed for osteoarthritis; for 3 days as needed for postoperative pain (first dose approximately two hours prior to surgery); with or without food
dose_regimen.quote: The recommended dosage of PREVICOX (firocoxib) for oral administration in dogs is 2.27 mg/lb (5.0 mg/kg) body weight once daily as needed for osteoarthritis and for 3 days as needed for postoperative pain and inflammation associated with soft-tissue surgery.

effectiveness.design: Negative-controlled (sham-dosed), double-blinded, multi-center field study (11 sites in France, Germany, Italy and USA) in 258 client-owned dogs undergoing abdominal or major external soft-tissue surgery; firocoxib 5.0 mg/kg PO about 2 h before surgery then once daily through Day 2 plus standard of care vs standard of care alone
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Success/failure defined by need for rescue analgesia (Glasgow Composite Pain Scale score of 8 or more, or investigator judgement)
effectiveness.result: 6.4% of firocoxib dogs vs 24.2% of control dogs needed rescue (p = 0.006); mean GCPS scores lower in the firocoxib group at every assessment (p < 0.05)
effectiveness.quote: Two hundred fifty-four dogs were included in the effectiveness analysis. The treatments were statistically significantly different (p = 0.006 from the generalized mixed model) with respect to the success/failure variable used as the definition of effectiveness. Eight out of 126 (6.40%) firocoxib-treated dogs and 31 out of 128 (24.2%) control dogs needed rescue medication, as shown in Table 1.

adverse_reactions.quote: Eight dogs (6.3%) in the firocoxib group (n = 127) experienced at least one adverse reaction compared with 10 dogs (7.6%) in the control group (n = 131), as shown in Table 2.

adverse_reactions.term: Vomiting (Table 2; columns firocoxib n (%), control n (%))

notes: Supplemental approval (2007) adding the soft-tissue surgery indication. One pivotal field study; dosage characterization and target animal safety are cross-referenced to the original 2004 NADA 141-230 approval (safety section is a short cross-reference and was not extracted). n_dogs given as group sizes because the total (254) appears only as words in the quote. No PK data. Additional Table 2 rows (SQ crepitus, swollen paw, puffy eyelids, SQ hemorrhage, suture site edema, facial edema, decompensated dilated cardiomyopathy; each 1 dog) omitted.

indication.text: Control of pain and inflammation associated with osteoarthritis and control of postoperative pain and inflammation associated with soft-tissue and orthopedic surgery in dogs (this supplement adds the orthopedic surgery indication).
indication.quote: PREVICOX Chewable Tablets are indicated for the control of pain and inflammation associated with osteoarthritis and for the control of postoperative pain and inflammation associated with soft-tissue and orthopedic surgery in dogs.

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: As needed for osteoarthritis; for 3 days as needed for postoperative pain (first dose approximately two hours prior to surgery); use the lowest effective dose for the shortest period
dose_regimen.quote: The recommended dosage of PREVICOX (firocoxib) for oral administration in dogs is 2.27 mg/lb (5.0 mg/kg) body weight once daily as needed for osteoarthritis and for 3 days as needed for postoperative pain and inflammation associated with soft-tissue and orthopedic surgery.

effectiveness.design: Double-blinded, multi-center (12 sites, USA and Europe) add-on field study with rescue: firocoxib 5.0 mg/kg PO about 2 h before surgery then once daily through Day 2 plus standard of care vs sham-dosed standard of care in dogs undergoing arthrotomy and joint stabilization (fabellar suture, fibular head transposition, TPLO, over-the-top)
effectiveness.n_dogs: 220 (116 PREVICOX, 104 control) in the effectiveness database; 226 in the safety database
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Success/failure based on completion of the study without rescue analgesia (GCPS score of 8 or more or investigator judgement)
effectiveness.result: Treatment failures 11.2% PREVICOX vs 37.5% control (p = 0.0050); least squares mean GCPS total scores lower with firocoxib (p < 0.05)

product_name: CLARO (florfenicol, terbinafine, mometasone furoate otic solution)

indication.text: Treatment of otitis externa in dogs associated with susceptible strains of Malassezia pachydermatis and Staphylococcus pseudintermedius.
indication.quote: CLARO is indicated for the treatment of otitis externa in dogs associated with susceptible strains of yeast (Malassezia pachydermatis) and bacteria (Staphylococcus pseudintermedius).

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: One dose per affected ear, administered by a veterinarian after cleaning the ear canal
dose_regimen.quote: Administer one dose (1 dropperette) per affected ear.

target_animal_safety.duration: Every 2 weeks on Study Days 1, 15 and 29 (three administrations) into both ear canals
target_animal_safety.n_animals: 12 male and 12 female treated plus 8 controls (4 male and 4 female)

findings.finding: All dogs survived; no clinically relevant effects on body weight, hearing or food consumption; post-treatment ear wetness/clear aural exudate
findings.quote: All dogs survived to scheduled necropsy. No clinically relevant treatment-related findings were noted in body weight, weight gain, hearing tests, or food consumption. Dogs administered CLARO were found to have post-treatment ear wetness or clear aural exudate.

findings.finding: Dose-dependent suppression of adrenal cortical response to ACTH stimulation at all dose levels, more pronounced on Day 30
findings.quote: There was dose-dependent suppression of the adrenal cortical response to ACTH-stimulation on both Days 2 and 30 of the dosing phase in all groups administered CLARO; this effect was more pronounced on Day 30 of the dosing phase.

findings.finding: Lower adrenal weight with cortical atrophy, higher liver/gall bladder weight with hepatocellular enlargement, decreased thymus weight
findings.quote: This was accompanied by lower group mean and individual adrenal gland weight and atrophy of the zona fasciculata/reticularis of the adrenal cortex. Higher group mean and individual animal liver/gall bladder weight parameters occurred with corresponding hepatocellular enlargement/cytoplasmic change. There was a decrease in thymus weight not associated with microscopic lymphoid depletion.

findings.finding: Hematology/chemistry shifts (neutrophils up in 5X males, lymphocytes and eosinophils down, AST up at all doses) within reference ranges
findings.quote: There was an increased group mean absolute neutrophil count in males in the 5X group, and decreased absolute lymphocyte and eosinophil counts, and increased AST in dogs administered CLARO at all dose levels.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Twenty-four Beagle dogs (12 male and 12 female), 12 weeks of age at enrollment, were administered CLARO and 8 dogs (4 male and 4 female) were administered a placebo control (saline).

effectiveness.design: Randomized (2:1), vehicle-controlled, multi-center (8 U.S. clinics) field study (P13-004) of a single 1 mL per ear administration after saline cleaning; 221 dogs enrolled (146 CLARO, 75 vehicle), 183 evaluable for effectiveness
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Treatment success on Day 30: total otitis externa clinical score of 3 or less (erythema, exudate, swelling, ulceration each 0-3) with no individual sign worsening
effectiveness.result: Success 72.5% CLARO vs 11.1% vehicle (P-value = 0.0001); effective against S. pseudintermedius (58 successes/16 failures) and M. pachydermatis (85/23)
effectiveness.quote: The effect iveness analysis included 120 dogs in the CLARO group and 63 dogs in the control group. T here were 87 successfully treated cases and 33 failures in the CLARO group, and 7 successes and 56 failures in the control group.

adverse_reactions.term: Abnormal integument (Table 4; columns CLARO N=146, control N=75)
adverse_reactions.quote: Abnormal integument (erythema, pyoderma, flea allergy dermatitis, pruritus, lipoma, etc.) 6 1

adverse_reactions.term: Adverse reactions directly attributable to CLARO (field study)
adverse_reactions.quote: There were also no adverse reactions directly attributable to administration of CLARO.

notes: Original approval (2015, corrected FOI summary). No PK section (topical otic product); an in vitro non-interference/MIC study is in the effectiveness section but not extracted as PK. Target animal safety quotes the GLP margin-of-safety study in 12-week-old Beagles (0X/1X/3X/5X of 1 mL/ear every 2 weeks x3); the control group received 5 mL/ear saline. The effectiveness quote reproduces OCR artefacts ('effect iveness', 'T here') verbatim. Adverse event rows are counts only (Table 4); remaining single-dog rows (cervical pain, diarrhea, lethargy, sneezing, trauma, tympanic membrane thickening, urinary incontinence, urinary tract infection) omitted.
